text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] Prometheus alert firing: prometheus_scrape_error_count > 0 for job=redwood-metrics (severity=P1) — some targets failing scrapes

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident #PD-19283 created and triggered to schedule (impact: degraded metrics ingestion)

alice.sre: ack'd PD-19283 - I'm taking on-call. seeing a bunch of `scrape_timeout` and `connect refused` in the prometheus targets UI.

alice.sre: quick check: `kubectl -n monitoring get pods` shows prom-0/1 healthy, but `prometheus` logs show repeated `context deadline exceeded` for `node-exporter` targets behind internal LB.

carla.infra: @alice.sre I can see increased 5xx from the metrics-proxy at the LB. Might be a scaling issue on the sidecar proxy pool. Investigating autoscaler.

alice.sre: hmm also seeing gaps in the inference-serving metrics `inference.requests_total` — panels dropping to 0 for some clusters. Could be scrape blackhole or the exporter crashed.

dave.obs: logs ingest shows backlog on `log-ingest-partition-7` lag ~ 120k msgs; consumer group `log-forwarder` is behind. Correlates with time of scrape failures ~ 07:12 UTC.

emma.support: any customer-facing impact? A few customers reported missing dashboards. Support ticket #6782 linked.

alice.sre: status update: running `curl -s http://prometheus-0.monitoring.svc:9090/-/targets` — about 6 targets down, mainly in `eu-west-1` and `us-west-2` inference pools.

carla.infra: autoscaler for metrics-proxy is stuck; horizontalpodautoscaler shows `DesiredReplicas 10 -> Current 3` due to failing HPA metrics. Scaling controller seems throttled. I'm going to manually scale the deployment to 10.

alice.sre: ok manual scale please. while that's happening, let's try increasing Prom scrape timeout to 30s for the job as a temporary mitigation (current 10s). patching `prometheus-rule.yml` now.

carla.infra: `kubectl -n monitoring scale deploy metrics-proxy --replicas=10` -> pods coming up. 6 new pods now running.

logs-bot: log-consumer lag metric alert cleared for partition 7? still showing 90k.

alice.sre: rolled scrape_timeout bump to 30s and reloaded Prom (`POST /-/reload`). rechecking targets... some are coming back healthy.

bob.sre: ping — can you confirm if the failures were network or CPU on the exporter instances? If it's network LB throttling we should consider increasing connect concurrency.

carla.infra: looking at LB metrics: backend 5xx spikes align with metrics-proxy restarts earlier (kubelet OOMKilled on a proxy pod). Node memory pressure on a few nodes in the region. I'm draining the worst offender nodes and cordoning to let new pods settle.

alice.sre: good. also re-enabled `inference` job `honor_labels` off in case label churn affected scraping. won’t change much but avoids some relabeling thrash.

dave.obs: log ingest lag slowly decreasing after scaling the consumers — now 48k. We triggered a temporary consumer replication to add throughput.

alice.sre: assessing customer impact: dashboards that rely on `inference.latency_p50` and `tokens_generated_total` were reporting zeros for ~20 minutes between 07:12–07:32 UTC in eu-west-1. This could affect internal alerting and customer dashboards but not inference itself.

emma.support: flagged the affected customers (5 customers across EU accounts). Sending initial advisory: "We observed delayed metrics and dashboard gaps for ~20 minutes; your inference API remained available. We'll follow up with root cause"

bob.sre: escalation: PD auto-escalated to SRE Lead 07:20 UTC. I'm on the thread. Are there any persistent errors after scale and timeout change?

alice.sre: still seeing a handful of targets flapping in us-west-2 (exporter connects succeed then time out). Running tcpdump on exporter pod to check connection patterns.

carla.infra: found kernel TCP ephemeral exhaustion on one older node group. Increasing `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` and `tcp_tw_reuse` on those nodes with a DaemonSet sysctl patch. Also migrating pods off that node pool.

alice.sre: tcp sysctl changes applied cluster-wide to the candidate nodes. Re-initiating `/-/targets` check... clean for most targets now.

logs-bot: log consumer lag now 6k and dropping.

alice.sre: moving to mitigation summary: 1) manually scaled metrics-proxy 2) increased Prometheus scrape timeout for `redwood-metrics` job to 30s 3) patched kernel TCP settings on older node pool 4) cordoned/drained memory-pressured nodes 5) spun up additional log consumer replicas to drain backlog

bob.sre: agreed. please prepare runbook steps and postmortem notes. Also we should add a follow-up to change HPA metrics to use stable signals not based on exported metrics that themselves can fail circularly.

emma.support: customer comms draft ready — sending to legal & trust for review.

alice.sre: handing off to @carla.infra for next 30m to watch autoscaler & consumer lag while I grab breakfast. I'll update PD incident with the mitigation steps.

pagerduty: PD-19283 status: acknowledged -> on-call assigned to alice.sre; escalated to bob.sre at 07:20 UTC; status updated to "mitigating".

incident-bot: Note: created incident post in #incidents with runbook link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/PD-19283

carla.infra: monitoring the cluster autoscaler logs and metrics-proxy error rate. consumer lag stable and trending to zero. I'll post final when it's fully caught up.

alice.sre: (07:45 UTC) confirmed: log lag cleared, Prom targets healthy, dashboards repopulated. closing PD after handoff.

bob.sre: recommend follow-up action items: - bake higher scrape_timeout as a configurable emergency setting - add synthetic exporter healthchecks upstream of HPA - schedule nodegroup upgrade to modern kernel - run a chaos job to validate exporter scale handling

emma.support: sent final customer update: "Issue resolved; dashboards delayed but inference API unaffected. Root cause: exporter/metrics proxy instability under node resource pressure. Next steps: infra improvements and additional monitoring."

alice.sre: closing notes: timeline and logs uploaded to incident page. tagging postmortem owner @bob.sre. thanks everyone :pray:

incident-bot: PD-19283 resolved at 07:48 UTC (duration ~36m).

carla.infra: final note — I'll keep an eye on autoscaler and create a follow-up ticket to prevent HPA throttling.

bob.sre: thanks team.
